title: Restricting mobile tracking can reduce fraud complaints through the data-resale chain
source_unit: NBER Working Paper 31692, revised May 2026; Apple App Tracking Transparency natural experiment, consumer fraud complaints, dark-web discussion, and sensitive-data prices
geography: United States; geographic and firm-risk variation around Apple mobile tracking restrictions

observations.period: Apple App Tracking Transparency natural experiment; working paper revised May 2026

denominator.unit: consumer fraud complaints and geographic/firm-risk comparisons; exact sample denominator is source-specific

fraud_complaints.unit: consumer fraud complaints after tracking and sharing restrictions

personal_information_misuse.unit: relative effect for complaints involving personal-information misuse

risky_data_practice_exposure.unit: effect heterogeneity in areas dominated by firms with riskier data practices

data_market_signals.value: dark-web discussion declined and sensitive-data prices increased

observations.method: Natural-experiment design leveraging Apple's App Tracking Transparency policy to examine tracking and sharing restrictions, consumer fraud complaints, geographic exposure to risky data practices, dark-web discussions, and prices for sensitive data.
observations.uncertainty: The paper is observational around a policy shock and the web page does not disclose one common denominator for all outcomes. Complaint reductions do not measure all fraud, unreported harm, reimbursement, account restoration, or trust. The supply-chain interpretation is supported by linked mechanism evidence but does not prove that every complaint or data-market change passed through the same route.
observations.subgroup: Consumers, complaint types involving personal-information misuse, areas with different exposure to risky data practices, and data-market indicators; these units should not be pooled into a single consumer-harm rate.
observations.counterinterpretation: Other contemporaneous changes in fraud, platform use, reporting, enforcement, or consumer behavior may contribute to the result. Tracking restrictions may shift fraud to other channels, impose matching or advertising costs, or affect groups differently depending on device access and alternative data sources.

boundary: This record adds a platform-data-control-to-consumer-fraud-consequence pathway. It does not establish a complete household fraud-recovery episode, universal privacy benefit, causal trust change, account restoration, reimbursement, or durable exit from data-dependent services.
